title: Extension views
description: What an extension draws (ui.render, ui.action): a View of sections of components, drawn by every app with its own design system. Also the assistant's persona-card, which joins the components in #1850.

Tone.description: A role color the app picks, never one of the extension's own. An unknown tone draws as neutral.

TextStyle.description: title and headline (UI version 6) are a section's big title and a small heading; an older app draws them as body.

FieldKind.description: date, time, datetime, multichoice and multiline are UI version 6. Values stay strings: date YYYY-MM-DD, time HH:MM (24 hours), datetime YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM local to context.tz, multichoice a JSON array of the chosen values, multiline the text with \n.

ChartKind.description: area, candlestick, donut and pie are UI version 6: an older app gets a line (an area, a candlestick's closes) or bars (a donut, a pie).

CandleRising.description: A candlestick's rising candle: green (the default) or red, as the market writes it; the falling one is the other.

Color.description: A named color (UI version 6): each app has its own of each, right in light and dark and in every style. Not a hex; an unknown one draws as the app's quiet ink. Only on badges, icons, tiles, chart series and sparks, never on text; never with a tone on the same object.

Placement.description: A slot in the apps an extension draws at (docs "UI slots"). extension_page is plugin_page's new name (UI version 3): the hub takes both and answers the new API with extension_page, the old one with plugin_page.

Size.description: How much room a view has: compact (a card), full (a page, a section), or for a widget the family it is drawn for (WidgetFamily).

WidgetFamily.description: A widget's size outside the app (docs "System placements"): a home screen widget's small / medium / large, a Lock Screen or watch face complication's accessory_*.

NavIcon.description: The fixed icon set: a nav_page's icon, a row's, an empty state's (UI version 3 for the last two and the icons after money; 4 for those after settings; 6 for those after file, and a metric's, a tile's, a row action's). Each app draws its own icon for the meaning; an unknown one draws as the default (extension; plugin is its old name).

state.description: The extension's own, sent back with the next render or action; at most 16 KB.

refresh_after.description: Draw again after this many seconds while on screen (30 at least; 0 never).

fallback.description: Plain text for an assistant card: required by CheckAssistantView; not required for extension views.

pages.description: Assistant card details keyed by page name; at most 8. A detail page cannot contain pages itself. Push.page refers to this root map.

key.description: Stable section identity in stream protocol 1 (UI version 7); optional for legacy snapshots.

Component.description: One component of a view, told apart by type. A type an app does not know is skipped and the rest drawn.

ProgressComponent.description: A bar filled to ratio (0 to 1).

RowComponent.description: A row of a list; with an action it can be tapped.

icon.description: At most one of icon, avatar and thumbnail.

control.description: A switch, a slider or a stepper; the row then has a key.

actions.description: Extra actions in the row's menu and under a swipe: shortcuts only, the same must be possible on the page the row opens.

ButtonComponent.description: A button; its title never wraps.

LinkComponent.description: A link the app opens inside itself: https only.

FieldComponent.description: An input; its value goes back under name when an action submits. A secret is never filled in.

earliest.description: date, time, datetime: the first one allowed, written like value.

latest.description: date, time, datetime: the last one allowed.

detail.description: A line of help under the field.

DividerComponent.description: A line between two groups of a section.

ChartComponent.description: A chart: bar, line, and in UI version 6 area, candlestick, donut, pie. Every series has the same labels in the same order; with more than one series each is named. A candlestick has one series whose points all have open, high, low and close (value is the close), at most 240 of them; a donut or a pie one series of 2 to 8 points.

center.description: donut: the words in the hole (a total).

rising.description: candlestick: the color of a rising candle.

StatGridComponent.description: A few numbers side by side.

SegmentedComponent.description: One of a few, chosen at once: its action goes with values {name: the chosen value}.

MarkdownComponent.description: Text in a safe subset of Markdown: headings (1 to 3), paragraphs, lists, bold, italics, inline code, code blocks, quotes, https links (opened in the app). No HTML, no images, no tables (a table is a table component). An older app gets it as plain text.

TableComponent.description: A table: 1 to 8 columns, at most 100 rows, each with as many cells as there are columns. Narrow screens scroll it sideways; cells never squeeze. An older app gets a row per line.

EmptyComponent.description: An empty state: nothing here yet, and maybe one thing to do about it. An older app gets a text and a button.

LoadingComponent.description: Loading: the extension answers it while its data comes, then sends ui.invalidate to be drawn again. An older app gets a quiet text.

HtmlComponent.description: Assistant only: self-contained HTML. Execution requires an isolated, network-denying renderer; unsupported clients show the root fallback. Extensions never execute it.

HeaderComponent.description: A detail page's head: a big title, state badges, a line of facts (author, branches, time, size). An older app gets a text and a row per fact.

BreadcrumbComponent.description: A path (repo / src / main.go): every crumb but the last may be tapped. An older app gets one text.

FileTreeComponent.description: Files as a tree the app builds from their paths (a directory with one child folds into a/b/c). action opens a file (values {path}); expand loads a directory given with no entries under it (values {path}). An older app gets a row per entry.

CodeComponent.description: A file's content: line numbers, the app's own syntax highlighting (language, else guessed from path), no wrapping. truncated with load: the rest comes from load (values {path, from: the next line}). An older app gets a code block.

line_url.description: An https link to lines of this file on its site, {start} and {end} standing for the lines (…/blob/<sha>/a.go#L{start}-L{end}).

DiffComponent.description: One file's diff: hunks of lines each starting with ' ', '+', '-' or '\'; unified or side by side is the app's choice. threads are inline comments at their lines; comment adds one (values {path, side, line, start_line?, body}); expand shows hidden lines between hunks (values {path, hunk, direction: up, down or all}); collapsed, or without hunks, it shows a button calling load (values {path}). An older app gets a code block.

context.description: Fetch hidden lines of the file (UI version 5): values {path, side: new or old, from, to: a line or end}; the extension answers with lines (ActionResult.lines), the page is not drawn again.

viewed.description: The user has marked this file viewed.

mark_viewed.description: Mark the file viewed or not: values {path, viewed: true or false}. Without it the app keeps viewed on the device, by path and revision.

revision.description: What this file's change is (a blob id): a viewed mark kept on the device holds for it only.

generated.description: A generated file or a lockfile: folded at first.

similarity.description: How alike a renamed file is to its old one, in percent.

draft.description: Add a comment to the pending review instead of sending it alone: values as comment's.

suggestions.description: The extension takes ```suggestion blocks in comments.

CommentThreadComponent.description: A discussion: comments in order (an event is drawn as a quiet line), and a reply box when reply is set (values {body}). An older app gets a row and a text per comment.

ComposerComponent.description: A multi-line input (Markdown) with a few buttons (comment, approve, request changes, merge): the one tapped sends the text as name, with the page's fields. An older app gets a field and a button each.

ImageComponent.description: A picture with an optional caption; tapping it shows it full screen unless no_zoom. A ref is the extension's own picture (a camera, a map) fetched through the hub. An older app gets a row with a thumbnail (url) or a line of text (ref).

alt.description: Read out, and shown when the picture does not load.

no_zoom.description: Tapping does nothing (else it shows the picture full screen).

GridComponent.description: Tiles in columns that fit the width: two on a phone, more on wider screens, at most max_columns (4 when absent). Each tile counts as a component of the page. An older app gets a row per tile.

CarouselComponent.description: Tiles in one line that scrolls sideways: cameras, rooms, a watchlist. Each tile counts as a component of the page. An older app gets a text (the title) and a row per tile.

ImageSource.description: Where a picture comes from (UI version 6): an https url the app loads without credentials, or a ref the extension serves itself (ui.image) through the hub; exactly one. path is written by the hub only, for a ref: its own address, which the app loads with its device credentials. An extension that writes path is refused.

ImageAspect.description: square 1:1, landscape 4:3 (the default), wide 16:9, portrait 3:4, auto from src's width and height (4:3 until the picture comes).

ImageFit.description: fill crops to fill the frame (the default); fit shows all of it.

RowControl.description: A control in a row or a tile (UI version 6). Changing it calls ui.action with action and values {name: the new value} (a switch "true" or "false", a slider and a stepper the number). The app shows the new value at once and puts back the old one if the action fails. A slider sends when the finger lifts, a stepper 0.6 s after the last tap.

step.description: More than 0 (checked by the hub); a slider's is (max - min) / 100 when absent.

display.description: How to write the value ("22.5 °C"); else the number and unit.

RowAction.description: One of a row's or a tile's extra actions (UI version 6): in its menu (long press, right click, the … button) and, with swipe, under a swipe from the trailing edge. confirm and push work as on any action; a destructive one has confirm.

swipe.description: Also under a swipe. At most two of a row's actions.

Spark.description: A small trend line inside a row, a metric, a stat or a tile (UI version 6): values only, no axes. Without color or tone, the app's quiet ink.

TileWidth.description: A carousel's tiles: narrow about 140pt (scenes), regular about 200pt (the default; rooms), wide about 80% of the screen (camera pictures).

Tile.description: A tile of a grid or a carousel (UI version 6): an icon or a picture, a title, a state line, a value; tapping does its action. active marks a tile that is on (a scene running, a light on) in its color.

icon.description: At most one of icon and image.

control.description: A switch only; the tile then has a key.

Layout.description: stack: sections one under another. split: on a wide screen the side pane's sections in a column at the start, the rest beside it, each scrolling on its own; on a narrow one the side pane folds into a bar on top that opens as a sheet.

Pane.description: Where a section of a split view goes.

Tabs.description: Tabs on top of the page (UI version 4): choosing calls ui.action with action and values {name: the value} (and the search's q). An older app gets a segmented, or buttons.

Fact.description: A label and its value in a header (Author · someone).

TreeEntry.description: A file (or a directory, kind dir) by its whole path from the root, / between names.

Hunk.description: A run of a diff: where it starts in the old and the new file, and its lines (' ' both, '+' new, '-' old, '\' a note such as no newline at end of file).

Thread.description: Inline comments at a line of a diff: line (and start_line for a range) on the side's numbering.

pending.description: A draft of the pending review, not sent yet.

resolve.description: Resolve or reopen: values {thread: id, resolved: true or false}.

Comment.description: A comment: its author, when (the app draws it relative), a body in the markdown subset, a badge (Approved). An event is a quiet line (merged, pushed two commits).

kind.description: Absent or action: a declared Action (action is its id). html: an HTML bridge reply (action is the html component's key, text the confirmed reply).

version.description: The card version the user saw and confirmed when this was committed; absent on records committed before #2019.

text.description: kind html only: the reply text the user confirmed.

ViewActionInput.description: The body of POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/views/{key}/actions. The reply text and form definition are read from the stored View, never from the client.

page.description: The named page the action is on; absent for the root page.

values.description: The fields this action submits, by name.

confirmed.description: The user confirmed the action's confirm prompt natively.

expected_version.description: The card version shown (and confirmed) to the user. Required when the action has confirm; a different stored version answers 409 view_changed.

AssistantHTMLActionInput.description: The body of POST /api/v1/assistant/conversations/{id}/views/{key}/html-actions: a persona.reply / persona.open call of a keyed html component, after the user confirmed it natively.

component_key.description: The key of the html component on that page of the stored card.

page.description: The named page the component is on; absent for the root page.

expected_version.description: The card version that ran the HTML and was shown in the confirmation.

text.description: reply only: the text shown in full in the confirmation.

url.description: open only: an https or supported persona:// target.

confirmed.description: Always true: the call was confirmed natively, outside the HTML.

AssistantHTMLOpenResult.description: What an html-actions open answers: the validated target to open inside the app, and the card version it was checked against.

ViewChangedError.description: 409 code view_changed: the stored card is not the version the user saw. Refresh, keep the draft and confirm again; never resubmit with the new version automatically.

view.description: The current card, as feed.views carries it (a transcript card: id is its key, version 1).

Action.description: What a row, a button or a segmented does: ui.action with its id. An object, so later kinds of action (push or pop a page) are fields added here.

confirm.description: Ask the user first, in these words.

submit.description: Send the page's fields as values.

reply.description: Assistant only: send this text back to the same conversation. The hub reads it from the saved view, not from the client.

open.description: Assistant only: an https URL or a validated persona/persona session, task, kb or file target, opened inside the app.

pop.description: Assistant only: return one page within the card.

push.description: Open a page on top of this one instead of calling ui.action (an app of UI version 3; an older one calls ui.action with id).

values.description: Values the action carries (UI version 4): sent with the page's and the component's values, these winning on a name they share. An older app sends none.

Push.description: A page pushed on the navigation stack: ui.render of the extension's ui (this one when empty; a full page: extension_page, plugin_page or nav_page) with state. title is shown until the view comes.

page.description: Assistant only: a page in the root View.pages. Never combined with ui or state.

Search.description: A search box on top of the page (UI version 3): the app calls ui.action with action and values {"q": the text}, 0.3 s after the user stops typing.

Filter.description: A drop-down beside the search box (UI version 3): choosing calls ui.action with action and values {name: the value} (and the search's q).

More.description: A section's last row, Load More (UI version 3): reaching it (or tapping it) calls ui.action with action once; the extension answers the whole view, longer.

Avatar.description: A person's or a chat's picture: an https image, else up to two characters drawn as the app's initials avatar.

ref.description: The extension's own picture (ui.image) through the hub, in place of url.

path.description: Written by the hub only, for a ref.

Thumbnail.description: A small picture at the row's start: an https image the app loads without any credentials, or (UI version 6) a ref the extension serves (ui.image) through the hub; exactly one of url and ref.

path.description: Written by the hub only, for a ref.

ChartSeries.description: One line, or one color of bars. No tone and no color: the app's own colors, in order. At most 120 points (240 for a candlestick, checked by the hub).

ChartPoint.description: A value at a label (a day, a model); display is how to write it ("¥1.20"), else the app writes value with the unit.

ActionResult.description: What ui.action answers: a new view, a short message, an https link to open, a page to push or to pop (UI version 3), or nothing (draw again).

push.description: Then open this page on top (after a submit: list, detail, edit).

pop.description: Then go back a page; the page below is drawn again.

lines.description: Lines of a file a diff's context asked for: the page is not drawn again.

items.description: Components to put in place of those with the same key on the page (each has a key): the rest is not drawn again.

FileLines.description: Lines of one side of a file from start (1 the first), as many as the extension has at hand (all of it, say); total is how many the file has.

Review.description: The pending review (UI version 5): a bar at the page's foot saying how many drafts there are, a summary box (name) and buttons (comment, approve, request changes) that send them all, discard throws them away. An older app gets a text and a composer on top.

PersonaCardKind.description: ring: one day's total and its parts (a donut); stacked_bar: parts side by side to compare (days, people).

PersonaCard.description: The assistant's ```persona-card block (#886): one JSON object. Joins the components in #1850; this form keeps drawing.
